bihar_raw_news.title: Message from alleged rigging in Bihar : Boycott elections - Frontline
bihar_raw_news.content: DIGITAL EXCLUSIVE CPI (ML)’s Bihar findings of rigging show why Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation is not enough And why the opposition should boycott elections to force electoral reform. Published : Oct 05, 2026 13:20 IST - 9 MINS READ Ajaz Ashraf AI Summary COMMents SHARE Copy link Email Facebook Twitter Telegram LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit READ LATER SEE ALL Remove CPI(ML) Liberation General Secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya and others stage a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision exercise, in Patna, Bihar, on Oct. 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI A day before protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar erupted in New Delhi and Mumbai on October 2, yet another allegation of election rigging surfaced—this time in Bihar. This allegation adds to the ever-growing claims of electoral fraud: Odisha and Andhra Pradesh in 2024, and West Bengal earlier this year. Yet Kumar’s resignation, even if it were to happen, would not restore the sanctity of elections. This is because the flawed electoral roll produced through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise will remain intact, as will the Modi government’s preponderant say in appointing commissioners to the Election Commission of India. As long as these two factors are in play, the participation of opposition parties in an electoral system rigged in BJP’s favour will only serve to legitimise it. But first, a look at the new claim of rigging from Bihar. Between June and September 2026, grassroots workers of the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) (Liberation) conducted surveys in which they found that nearly 17 per cent of those deleted from the voter list as of June 24, 2025, the day the decision to conduct the SIR was announced, had been wrongfully removed. It was wrongful because the voters were alive and living during the SIR process, as they still are now, at the addresses given in the June 24 voter list. The CPI(ML) Liberation made this startling discovery after tracking 9,288 voters in 50 booths spread across 10 of the 20 constituencies the party contested in the 2025 Assembly election. These voters had been deleted from either the draft or the final rolls during the SIR process. Of them, 17 per cent had not shifted from their residences—yet they were expunged from the list the SIR produced. In Bihar, a total of 68.66 lakh voters were deleted during the SIR. If this 17 per cent is extrapolated across the State, it would mean 11.36 lakh voters were denied their constitutional right to vote. The impact these illegitimate deletions had on the election results was likely enormous. For instance, the BJP polled 0.06 per cent more votes than the CPI(ML) Liberation to win the Agiaon Assembly seat, where 10 per cent of deleted voters, registered in four booths, were deemed illegitimate—and could not therefore exercise their franchise. bihar_raw_news.title: Essential Drug List Revised to Improve Healthcare Access in Bihar - The Indian Practitioner
bihar_raw_news.content: Medi News Facebook Twitter Linkedin The Bihar health department has revised its Essential Drug List to include specialised medicines and medical devices for conditions such as haemophilia, heart attacks, kidney disease, cervical cancer and rabies. The move aims to improve access to treatment at government hospitals and reduce patients’ out-of-pocket expenses. Key Additions to the List The revised list includes Factor VIII medicines for haemophilia and von Willebrand disease. It also adds 16 medical devices and consumables for dialysis, including dialysers, blood lines and fistula needles. In addition, hospitals will have access to Pap smear kits for cervical cancer screening and Karman cannulas for safe abortion services. Wider Access to Emergency Treatment The government has also expanded the availability of Tenecteplase, an emergency medicine used to treat heart attacks, to district hospitals, community health centres and notified trauma centres. As per The Times of India, the revised list also includes new options for rabies treatment and an updated inhalation medicine for asthma and COPD. Also Read | RCML Strengthens Telangana Presence with Majority Stake in Prashanthi Hospital Focus on Affordable Healthcare Health Minister Nishant Kumar said the revision will help government hospitals provide better treatment, particularly for poor and needy families. Therefore, the move could improve access to essential healthcare while reducing the financial burden on patients.

bihar_raw_news.title: RBI Repo Rate Hike 2026: Why RBI May Raise Rates Amid Oil Price Risks - Jagran Josh
bihar_raw_news.content: RBI MPC Meet Begins Today: Will the Rate-Cut Cycle End With First Repo Rate Rise Since 2023? Check Expected Hike By Jaisal Kaur Last Updated: Oct 5, 2026, 12:07 IST The repo rate presently stands at 5.25 per cent. If the RBI raises it by 25 basis points, the rate would move to 5.50 per cent. This would be the first repo rate hike since February 2023, when the central bank increased the rate to 6.50 per cent. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is meeting from October 5 to 7, with the policy decision due on October 7. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is widely expected to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points in its October monetary policy review, potentially resulting in a reversal of the rate-cut cycle that started in 2025. The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is meeting from October 5 to 7, with the policy decision due on October 7. The repo rate presently stands at 5.25 per cent. If the RBI raises it by 25 basis points, the rate would move to 5.50 per cent. This would be the first repo rate hike since February 2023, when the central bank increased the rate to 6.50 per cent. Why Is the RBI Considering a Rate Hike? A major concern is the renewed escalation in West Asia and its impact on global crude oil prices. India imports a large share of its crude oil requirements, making higher energy prices a potential source of inflationary pressure. The RBI's August policy had assumed an oil price of around $90 per barrel for 2026-27. However, crude prices have since moved above that level, with economists warning that a sustained increase could push up transportation, fuel and production costs. Higher crude prices can also create second-round inflationary effects as businesses pass increased input and transportation costs on to consumers. Inflation Risks Are Rising Retail inflation has also been bolstered. India's consumer price inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August, compared with 4.45 per cent in July, remaining above the RBI's 4 per cent medium-term target for a third consecutive month. Economists observed that food inflation has gained momentum, while core inflation and services inflation have also shown signs of strengthening. Higher input costs have already prompted some automobile manufacturers to announce price increases, while other consumer-goods companies could face similar pressures. RBI on Economic Growth The rate decision comes despite strong economic activity. The RBI had projected real GDP growth for 2026-27 at 6.7 per cent, but several economists expect the central bank to revise its growth forecast upwards because of stronger-than-expected activity. Some estimates put the revised forecast above 7 per cent. Strong growth gives the RBI more room to prioritise inflation control without adding monetary support. Could More Rate Hikes Follow? Market expectations suggest the October move could be followed by another 25-basis-point increase in December if crude prices remain elevated. bihar_raw_news.title: Sharad Sagar US journey: 'Bihari in me said I'll come back when your President invites me'
bihar_raw_news.content: ET Online Sharad Sagar founded Dexterity Global For Sharad Vivek Sagar , returning to Bihar after studying in the US was not supposed to be the obvious career move. His American friends could see what he was apparently walking away from, a job in Manhattan, a large salary, a corporate career and the lifestyle that came with it. Sagar, however, was more interested in what he could build back home. When they asked him when he planned to return to the US, he gave them an answer that, at the time, was meant partly in jest. He would come back when the US President invited him. Years later, that is almost exactly what happened. Sagar has now revisited the story in an Instagram video, recalling how a decision that baffled his friends eventually led him back to the US for an invitation from the White House. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sharad Vivek Sagar (@sharadsagar) Sharad Sagar's unusual answer to his American friends Sagar was studying in the US when he began thinking about returning to India. His friends reportedly found the idea difficult to understand. Why leave after getting an American education? Why return without first earning a sizeable salary? And why give up the possibility of working from a Manhattan high-rise? Sagar remembers them questioning his decision in blunt terms. “You just received such a great education and you're going back without earning money and like working out of a Manhattan high-rise building, getting those fat paychecks, driving those German cars,” he recalled in the video. Live Events They also wanted to know when he would come back to America. That was when Sagar gave them the answer that would acquire an entirely different meaning years later. “And the Bihari I was, I would tell them, I would come back when your president invites me,” he said. At the time, there was no obvious reason to believe that would happen. The invitation that changed the punchline In September 2016, Sagar was in West Bengal when an email arrived early in the morning. It was around 5 am, he recalled, when he received an invitation from the White House. “In September, around that time, I was in the state of West Bengal. That morning at 5 a.m., I received an invite from the White House saying that the president would like to invite me to a special gathering of leaders,” Sagar said. The invitation came from the administration of US President Barack Obama. Sagar was invited to South by South Lawn : A White House Festival of Ideas, Art and Action, held at the White House on October 3, 2016. The event was designed to bring together people involved in ideas, creativity, innovation and initiatives intended to make a social impact. For Sagar, the invitation had an additional distinction. He recalled being the only Indian invited to the gathering. “I was the only Indian invited, and it was just such a remarkable honour,” he said.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar's Mokama bridge commissioned after safety clearance, doubling rail capacity across Ganges
bihar_raw_news.content: The new bridge is designed to accommodate speeds of up to 140 kmph and will be integrated with the Mokama-Barauni section and the Howrah-Delhi main line. (Pic Credit: @AshwiniVaishnaw/X) News Brief Bihar's Mokama Bridge Commissioned Today After Safety Clearance, Doubling Rail Capacity Across The Ganga By Arjun Brij Published: 5th Oct, 2026 at 12:03 PM A new double-line rail bridge over the Ganges at Mokama began operations early this morning, with the Mahananda Express becoming the first train to cross. The train crossed the bridge at approximately 90 km per hour, marking a significant improvement over the 40-50 kmph speed restrictions on the existing Rajendra Setu. The Rs 2,400 crore infrastructure project adds two rail lines alongside the existing single-line Rajendra Setu, increasing capacity on a crucial railway corridor linking north and south Bihar. Built parallel to the decades-old bridge, the new structure spans approximately 1.86 km, whilst the overall project extends to around 14 km including connecting tracks and associated infrastructure. Guru Prakash, Commissioner of Railway Safety for the Eastern Circle in Kolkata, conducted a two-day safety inspection on 3 and 4 October before granting clearance. The inspection covered the bridge structure, tracks, signalling systems, electrification facilities and other technical arrangements across the Rajendra Pul-Hathidah Upper-Rampur Dumra rail section. The project, which was sanctioned in the 2015-16 Rail Budget and construction work launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in March 2016, includes three new electronic interlocking systems, two interlocked level-crossing gates and an automatic signalling system. IRCON International awarded the construction contract to Afcons Infrastructure on an engineering, procurement and construction basis. The new bridge is designed to accommodate speeds of up to 140 kmph and will be integrated with the Mokama-Barauni section and the Howrah-Delhi main line. The existing Rajendra Setu will continue handling train operations, taking the total number of rail lines across the Ganges on this section to three. The commissioning comes ahead of the Diwali and Chhath festival period, when rail traffic to Bihar typically increases substantially. bihar_raw_news.title: Geoeconomics Expert Suzuki highlights Mumbai-Ahmedabad train project importance ... - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Geoeconomics Expert Suzuki highlights Mumbai-Ahmedabad train project importance for Japan-India ties Updated: 1 day, 1 hour ago New Delhi, October 04, 2026(ANI): Speaking on bilateral economic cooperation, high-technology partnerships, and infrastructure development at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave, Institute of Geoeconomics Director Kazuto Suzuki said, "...Japan and India have been engaging in a lot of economic projects. The high-speed train from Mumbai to Ahmedabad is one big project. The success of this high-speed train is going to be the sort of icebreaker between Japan and India. Also, in space, there's a lot of collaboration in satellite projects and moon exploration. In terms of semiconductors, Japan is now reaching out to various economic entities in India, including Tata Semiconductor and Tata Electronics, to build a factory in the state of Gujarat, and it is very much an increasing opportunity for Japan and India to cooperate in the high-technology sector... Japan and India have been working in cooperation to support the buildup of the Indian semiconductor industry. Regarding electric vehicles, Japan has not invested as heavily as other countries like China or European automakers; Japan has been focusing on hybrid cars. I assume that hybrid cars are coming into India, and because of the lack of infrastructure, I think hybrid cars have certain advantages, at least for the next decade, to be a major carbon-reduction automobile transportation means..." national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin will hold bilateral discussions in New Delhi today. President Parmelin will be on a three-day state visit to India, accompanied by a high-level delegation comprising senior officials and business leaders. Prime Minister Modi and President Parmelin will review progress in bilateral cooperation across a wide range of areas, including trade and investment, science, technology and innovation, mobility, culture, and people-to-people contact. The leaders will also exchange views on regional and global developments, including cooperation in multilateral fora. President Parmelin will meet President Droupadi Murmu this evening. External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar will also call on President Parmelin. Akashvani correspondent reports that this is President Parmelin’s first state visit to India and second visit this year. Earlier, in February, the Swiss President visited India to participate in the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi. The visit assumes added significance in view of his participation in the 2nd India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on the 7th of this month to mark the first anniversary of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement coming into force. Among EFTA countries, Switzerland is the largest trade and investment partner of India. India and Switzerland share longstanding friendly relations. This visit will further strengthen bilateral relations, building upon the regular high-level exchanges and deepen cooperation in new areas of mutual interest.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 81 Flydubai flight’s Omani co-pilot tried to crash aircraft in Saudi desert after hijack attempt foiled
national_raw_news.content: Flydubai flight’s Omani co-pilot tried to crash aircraft in Saudi desert after hijack attempt was foiled, reports Italian newspaper Corriere Della Sera. The paper says, Omani co-pilot Hammam al-Hammami attacked Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar to take control of the plane and crash it into a building at Tel Aviv in Israel. Al-Hammami’s original plot was to kill Flight Captain Smit Machchhar, fly the plane to Tel Aviv, and crash it into one of the city’s skyscrapers, the report claimed, citing Israeli intelligence. According to the newspaper, Hammami realised his original plan could not be carried out, so he decided to crash the plane in the desert. He switched off the autopilot and pushed the control stick. Within 30 seconds, the aircraft lost 16,000 feet of altitude and was on its way to hit the ground. Al-Hammami tried to damage the controls of the aircraft as well before the passengers overpowered him. Yaniv Hayoun, a plumber by profession, pulled the control stick towards him and prevented the plane from losing altitude further. Later, the two off-duty pilots took control of the aircraft. The pilots safely landed the plane. Captain Smit Machchhar was rushed to the hospital, and his co-pilot was handed over to the authorities in Saudi Arabia. Israel has described the incident as a terror attack and is probing how a pilot from Oman — with whom Israel has no diplomatic relations — was cleared to fly into Tel Aviv, flouting its security policy.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Sports 66 India signs off with 85 medals after Gold rush in cricket, hockey & Kabaddi at Asian Games
national_raw_news.content: India concluded its campaign at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya with 85 medals, including 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze, finishing fourth in the overall standings. India’s 2026 Asian Games campaign produced a series of landmark achievements across disciplines. The defining feature of India’s campaign was its clean sweep of gold medals in men’s and women’s cricket, kabaddi and hockey. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games concluded yesterday, bringing more than two weeks of exciting sporting action to an end. In cricket, India retained both titles. The women’s team defeated Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final, while the men’s team overcame Pakistan by 19 runs to complete the golden double. Kabaddi also produced a clean sweep. The women’s team defeated Iran 37-34 to successfully defend its title, while the men came from behind to beat Iran 40-34. Hockey also completed the sweep. The Indian women ended a 44-year wait for an Asian Games medal by defeating China 1-0, with Lalremsiami scoring the decisive goal in the 10th minute. It was India’s first women’s hockey gold at the Asian Games since 1982. The men’s team defeated Malaysia 5-1 to retain its title and claim India’s fifth men’s hockey gold, following triumphs in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022. It was also the first time India’s men’s and women’s hockey teams won gold at the same Asian Games. Both teams secured qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. Archery was one of India’s most successful disciplines, producing nine medals – five gold, two silver and two bronze. Boxing produced India’s best Asian Games campaign in terms of gold medals, with three gold and three bronze medals. Indian wrestlers won six medals – two gold, two silver and two bronze, making it the country’s best Asian Games wrestling tally since Jakarta 1962.
